newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short-term swaps up, depos flat in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek short-term swaps up, depos flat in late trade.

text.p: Greek interbank deposits were stable in late trade and short-term forex forwards were up with implied drachma rates around 11.30 percent, dealers said.
"Interbank deposits are steady," a state bank dealer said. "There was thin trading activity in forex forwards, but only short-term rates rose," he said.
"There was nothing particular happening on Friday. There were some price inquiries. Taxable bonds of January 28 were in demand," the dealer said.
Ecu/drachma was down between 303.85 to 303.90 in late trade after opening at 303.90, an ABN AMRO Bank treasury sales officer said.
"Trading was rangebound and choppy. This was a quiet day with only some ecu selling in the morning," she said.
The mark was quoted at 156.48/58 from Friday's 156.640 fix, the dollar at 263.91/01 drachmas from 264.250 and the Ecu at 303.78/88 from 303.950 drachmas.
